title: Control knot memo: quick triage + evidence notes
content:
Purpose: quick, messy capture of control tangles I ran into during initial evidence sweep for SOC2 prep. Not polished — notes to self and two collaborators. Use to pick up where I left off.

Top-level worries (short):
- Key rotation evidence: KMS rotation is configured, but exported snapshot for audit only shows key policy changes (no rotation metadata in UI) — need CloudTrail filter query.
- S3 log retention: some buckets for model artifacts had lifecycle rules but I found older objects in 'redwood-model-backups' older than retention target. Who ran ad-hoc copy?
- Private VPC deployment traces: Private control plane logs are in customer-managed S3; useful but access pattern for our infra team is messy. Need an access play to capture consistent exports.

Notes + rough action items:
- KMS / key rotation
  - Evidence that rotation exists: screenshot of KMS keys list + KMS key policy + a CloudTrail query showing RotateKey operation.
  - TODO: write CloudTrail saved query (Maya) to pull RotateKey events for last 12 months. Put query id in audit folder.
  - Quick test: schedule a rotation on staging CMK, confirm CloudTrail entry and then roll back (or record) steps for the audit runbook.

- S3 / artifact retention
  - Found objects dated 2024-11 in 'redwood-model-backups' that should have been pruned by 180d rule. Hypothesis: lifecycle rule scope limited by prefix; backup process uses different prefix.
  - Action: run lifecycle-report script (infra repo: scripts/lifecycle-report) for all buckets with 'model' in name. Omar to run and drop CSV in linked_artifacts.
  - Evidence: lifecycle config screenshot + CSV of objects older than policy.

- Access reviews / IAM
  - Permanent service account: 'svc-model-importer' has wide s3:* permissions. Need to map which pipelines require this vs ad-hoc jobs.
  - Suggested mitigation: create narrower role for imports with scoped prefixes. Work with platform-eng to plan cutover (canary config).
  - Evidence: IAM role bindings + last-used timestamp for credentials (IAM access advisor).

- Private / VPC controls
  - Some customers run private deployments with customer-managed logging. For audit we need signed attestation that logs exported or an internal check showing our aggregator pulled copies.
  - Pattern: ask SE to request customer proof OR provide a copy-of-export if customer gives permission; log access is sensitive — add template language to customer privacy addendum.

- Observability / console data retention
  - Console stores per-route traces for 90 days by default. For SOC2 we may need to produce examples of trace retention policy and a sample export.
  - Note: there is an internal toggle for retention extension on Dedicated customers — need a short doc showing default + exceptions.

Evidence capture checklist (messy):
- [ ] CloudTrail saved query for KMS RotateKey events (Maya)
- [ ] Screenshot of KMS key details (Ida)
- [ ] Lifecycle config screenshots + object list CSV (Omar)
- [ ] IAM binding export for svc-model-importer + access advisor output (Ida)
- [ ] Console retention doc draft (Maya)
- [ ] Private deployment attestation template draft (legal + SE)

Open questions / discussion prompts (for next sync):
- Are we comfortable relying on customer-supplied logs for Private control evidence? If so, need standard template and minimal fields (timestamp, requester, sha256 of file) so audit can verify authenticity.
- For S3 lifecycle mismatch: do we accept a manual cleanup + auditor note, or do we have to prove the rule prevented deletion? (I think prove: run lifecycle-report retroactively.)
- Should we centralize evidence artifacts in a single bucket with restricted access (pros: consistent; cons: PII/payload handling risk)?

Quick snippets to copy into Confluence later: 
- "Evidence group: key-management" -> list: KMS policy, CloudTrail saved query, rotation runbook, staging rotation screenshot.
- "Evidence group: storage-retention" -> list: lifecycle config, object-exception CSV, backup job config link, owner contact.

Random micro findings (notes-to-self):
- The RBAC role used by the legacy import lambda is hard-coded in terraform at infra/legacy-lambdas/main.tf line ~73. If we rotate that role, the import will fail — coordinate with infra team.
- There is an email thread (slack: #platform ops, 2025-12-11) about ad-hoc backups using 'sync' job run by oncall; archive that thread for context.
- Model artifact backups include some PII fields in metadata? Confirm. If true, flag for legal and redact examples used as evidence.

Meeting notes (23 Feb quick sync):
- Platform-eng: will provide lifecycle-report CSV by 2026-02-28.
- SE: will ask two customers for private logs attestation templates by 2026-03-10.
- Trust-ops: compile evidence bundle and propose scope for the auditor by 2026-03-15.

Next small steps (for me):
1) Draft CloudTrail saved query and paste into this doc.
2) Take KMS screenshots in staging and upload to /evidence/kms-rotations/2026-03-04/
3) Follow up with Omar on lifecycle CSV (ping on Slack).

That's enough for now — messy but captures the knot. Will prune into Confluence when we have artifacts.

Ida
